questions.q: What do we call the common starting point where two rays meet to form an angle?
questions.a: It is called the vertex. A wrong answer (like "corner" or "point") shows the student is not using the correct geometric vocabulary needed for formal construction.

questions.q: If two different angles have the same degree measure, but one has very long arms and the other has very short arms, which angle is larger?
questions.a: They are equal. A wrong answer reveals the common misconception that longer arms make an angle "bigger" because the student is confusing physical length with the measure of rotation.

questions.q: If an angle measures 95°, how would you classify it: acute, right, or obtuse?
questions.a: It is an obtuse angle. A wrong answer suggests the student hasn't memorized the ranges (Acute < 90°, Right = 90°, Obtuse > 90° and < 180°).

questions.q: Why do we have two sets of numbers (scales) on a standard protractor?
questions.a: To measure angles opening in either direction (left or right). A wrong answer shows the student doesn't understand how to align the protractor with the base ray.

questions.q: Can a reflex angle be measured using a standard semi-circle protractor? If so, how?
questions.a: Yes, by measuring the interior angle and subtracting it from 360°, or by measuring the "gap" and adding 180°. A wrong answer indicates difficulty in visualizing the full 360° rotation.

questions.q: Draw a rough sketch of an angle that is exactly 45°. How would you explain to a friend that this is half of a right angle?
questions.a: The answer should describe that since a right angle is 90°, and 45° is 90° divided by 2, they represent the same "turn." An answer that focuses only on drawing without explaining the relationship lacks conceptual depth.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: An angle is the amount of ______ between two rays that share a common starting point, called the vertex.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are opening a pair of scissors; as the blades move apart, the ______ between them grows—that "opening" is an angle.
Fill in the blank: Angles are measured in degrees (°), where a full turn is ______°.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can identify the vertex and arms of an angle, classify it by type (acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex), and measure it accurately using a protractor.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you are opening a pair of ______; as the blades move apart, the space between them grows—that "opening" is an angle.
